translate_en|mods/Fletcher/42/media/lua/: No rounds yet. Ten arrows at a target within 20 tiles make a round.
A stave was cut from this tree lately. Give it a few days.
Needs an axe to cut a limb.
Needs a sharp knife to shape it.
No tree to cut it from.
You don't know how to make a longbow stave yet.
Too slow: the lob's power is gone
On the club board at number %1.
Straw, no score  (arrow %1 of 10, %2 so far)
You nock faster with a quiver worn: the arrow comes up already turned the right way.
You can hold a full draw half again as long before your arm starts to shake.
Your shots carry less far: a waxed string, a padded shelf, no slap of the arrow on the riser.
Fewer of your arrows break: you pull them straight out and shoot where they'll land soft.
Your shots stray less: anchor the same way every time and let the string go, don't pluck it.
Set the loaded crossbow down facing where you face, with a wire run out about 5 tiles ahead. The first zombie to walk into the wire takes the bolt. Uses one twine, wire or fishing line.
Cock it and load a bolt first.
Needs twine, wire or fishing line.
Shooting and making bows and arrows. A faster draw, a steadier aim, quicker nocking and fewer broken arrows.
Cut Arrow Shafts from a Stick
Rip Large Plank into Arrow Shafts
Strap Army Angle-head Flashlight to Bow
Thanks for watching. Now go shoot.
Always string it with your legs, not your arms. You'll thank me when your back doesn't go out.
I'm Ray Dunbar. Shoot straight, and I'll see you next time.
Fifty arrows a day, every day, and you'll be surprised how fast it comes.
Don't yank the string loose. Just relax your fingers and let the bow do the work.
Every good shot is the same shot. Same stance, same draw, same anchor, same release.
Behind the shoulder, not the head. The big target is the sure target.
Kentucky bowhunter Ray Dunbar walks you through your first season with a bow: picking one, stringing it, and making that first clean shot.
Three fingers on the string: one above the arrow, two below. That's your Mediterranean draw.
Ray Dunbar returns for the advanced course: shooting at range, moving targets, broadheads, and making every arrow count.
Go find your arrows after. Good arrows are worth walking for.
Howdy, folks. Ray Dunbar here, and today we're going bowhunting.
VHS: Traditional Archery: Form and Release
Missed? Don't move. Nock another one, nice and slow. A quiet miss is a second chance.
Stand sideways to the target. Feet about shoulder width. Like you're waiting for a bus.
Watch the bow arm here in slow motion. Locked, but not stiff. The elbow rolls out of the string's way.
Ray Dunbar again. If you've watched the first tape, you're ready for the hard part.
Moving target? Lead it. Swing with the animal and release while you're still swinging.
A gun gets one shot before every critter in the county knows where you are. A bow gets as many as you've got arrows.
That's the beauty of a bow, folks. Quiet as a church mouse.
[Slow-motion footage of an arrow flexing as it leaves the bow]
A good stave of hickory or ash, a sound string, and some patience. That's a bow.
If your arm is shaking at full draw, let down. A tired shot is a wasted arrow.
VHS: Bowhunting Basics with Ray Dunbar
Broadheads hit hard but they fly different. Practice with what you hunt with.
Hold your form until the arrow lands. Peeking early pulls the shot.
Check every arrow when you pick it up. A cracked shaft can come apart on the string.
Draw with your back, not your bicep. Squeeze those shoulder blades together.
A tight grip torques the bow, and the arrow goes left. Every time.
Now, a lot of fellas think you need a two-hundred dollar bow to get started. You don't.
That's it for the advanced course. Stay patient, stay quiet, and you'll eat well.
Welcome. I'm Linda Pryor, and this tape is about one thing: a repeatable shot.
Beginners grip the bow like a hammer. Let it sit in the web of your hand instead.
Coach Linda Pryor of the Louisville Archery Club breaks down the shot, from stance to follow-through, with slow-motion footage.
Pull back to the same spot on your face every single time. Corner of the mouth works for me.
That spot's called your anchor. No anchor, no accuracy. Simple as that.
Wind in your face. Always. They can't hear you, but they sure can smell you.
See that? No bang, no echo. The deer two trees over didn't even look up.
Now the release. The string hand moves straight back, past your ear. That's your follow-through.
VHS: The Silent Hunter: Advanced Bowhunting
Out past twenty yards, that arrow is dropping. Aim a touch high and learn your bow.
Archery's own XP multiplier, used when the global XP multiplier is turned off (per-skill multipliers), like every vanilla skill's.

How far flying arrows and bolts stray from where you aim. 1 is the default. Lower is more precise (0.5 halves the spread), higher is wilder (2 doubles it). The aiming reticle follows it. Archery level, steady aim, moving and moodles still apply on top.
Multiplies every bomb arrow's blast damage (Blasting, Shrapnel, Concussion and Sticky): 1 is normal (a pipe bomb is about 1.5), 0 harmless.
Incendiary Arrows start fires. Unticked: they don't go off (no fire from any arrow but the plain fire arrow). The server's own no-fire setting also stops them.

Bomb arrows (Blasting, Shrapnel, Concussion, Sticky, Incendiary and Smoke) go off where they land, and Explosives Diagrams can teach how to make them. Unticked: they never go off, and diagrams teach only the game's own recipes.
How often bows, crossbows and boxes of arrows or bolts turn up in the world: 1 is normal, 0 none (craft everything yourself), up to 4. Hunter zombies with bows have their own setting.
Percent of hunter zombies that carry a bow or crossbow on their back. Rangers and survivalists sometimes do too. 0 turns it off.
Fire Arrows: Light By Hand (Off: Light On Release)

Ticked: you light each fire arrow yourself. With it nocked, hold R (RB on a controller) and choose Light Arrow, with a lighter or matches; it burns for about 25 seconds, and if you don't shoot in time the rag burns away and a plain arrow is left. A fire arrow shot without lighting it doesn't burn anything. Unticked: fire arrows light themselves as you shoot, if you carry a lighter or matches (one use per arrow).
Arrows and bolts loosed while sneaking at a zombie that hasn't noticed you hit 20 percent harder and are more likely to be critical hits (more with the Sneaking skill). Flying arrows only.

Arrows and bolts fly as real projectiles: they drop over distance, stop at walls and trees, and hit whatever they reach first, with headshots by height. Off: every shot hits or misses at once like a gun.

Harder shots earn more Archery XP (long shots, lobs, headshots, moving targets, a quick release...), and bomb and fire arrows earn a share of a kill for each zombie they kill, up to a limit. Easy shots pay less as Archery rises, and so do repeated hits on the same zombie. Off: every hit pays the same, as before 0.12.
A straw bale with a painted face. Put it down and shoot at it: arrows stick in the straw without breaking, and you learn from every hit until Archery 3.

Worn across the back, with a bow on your back or a backpack if you like. Holds only arrows and bolts, and many more than the hip quiver. Arrows come from the hip quiver first; nocking from the back quiver is a little faster than from a bag.
A fletcher's workbench with a jig and a vise: fletch arrows and bolts five at a time, faster, as matched sets that fly truer and break less.

A pipe charge on a heavy shaft, with an impact fuze. It explodes where it strikes, killing almost anything within about 3 tiles, you included, and every zombie for a long way hears it. Heavy: it flies slower and not as far. The fuze only arms after about 5 tiles, so closer than that it's a dud. Walls and closed doors stop the blast. Used up when it goes off.
A sawn length of pipe packed with gunpowder and capped. One goes on a Blasting Arrow.
A bow-length strip sawn from a plank. Lumber is already dry: string it as it is.
A light made for a compound bow, on a short stabilizer. Brighter and lighter than a flashlight taped on, and barely slows your aim. Fits the Compound Bow. Takes batteries.
Stand it within 20 tiles of an Archery Target. Ten arrows at the target make a round out of 100, and the best ten rounds go up on the board by name. Right-click it to read it.

An aerosol can wrapped in aluminium on a heavy shaft, set off by an impact fuze. A small blast, a deafening bang that draws zombies from far away, and zombies within about 4 tiles are knocked off their feet. For breaking up a crowd, not for killing. The fuze arms after about 5 tiles.
Bent shaft, torn fletching: it won't fly true. Re-fletch it with one Fletching to shoot it again.
Its vanes are torn: re-fletch it with one Fletching to shoot it again.

A fuel-soaked rag behind the point. Carry a lighter or matches and it is lit as you loose it: it sets alight whatever it hits, or starts a fire where it lands, and burns away. Fires spread: mind the grass and your own walls.
A barbed arrow on a fishing line. Aim at fishable water and watch for fish breaking the surface: shoot one as it rises and reel it in. Missed shots are reeled back. Choose it from the reload menu.

A road flare taped over the point, struck as you loose it. It lights where it lands, or the zombie it hits, bright red for about a minute, and never starts a fire. It hisses while it burns, and zombies nearby come to see. Spent once it lands.
Green wood. Lay it on a Stave Rack to season it (a bow stave takes 3 days, a longbow stave 5): a bow from seasoned wood hits harder, reaches farther and wears slower.
Cook it on a stove or campfire for about an hour, then pour off the glue.
Pour it off to get a tube of glue and your pot back.
Worn on the right hip. Holds only arrows and bolts; nocking or cocking from it is faster.
A nail striker over a shotgun-shell primer: it sets the charge off when the arrow strikes.

A can of petrol with a rag wick on a heavy shaft. Light it first, like a fire arrow: where it lands it bursts into a ring of fire about 3 tiles across. Fire spreads: keep it away from your own walls. Unlit, it's a dud. Heavy: it flies slower and not as far.
Holds an arrow shaft while its fletching sets, so every vane sits the same. Part of a Fletcher's Bench.
One of a matched set made at a Fletcher's Bench: strays less and breaks less than an ordinary arrow.
A note rolled round the shaft behind a rubber blunt. Write the note first. Wherever the arrow lands, the note is left there for whoever finds it: a rooftop, a fenced yard, a window you can't reach.
A rattling can on a blunt arrow. Wherever it lands it makes a racket for a few seconds that draws zombies within about 18 tiles: shoot it away from you to pull a crowd off your path. Barely hurts.
A stiff arrow shaft with a socket and oversized vanes, made to carry a payload: the base of the Blasting and Incendiary Arrows.
Fletching cut from plastic. Arrows fletched with it last longer and break less, but stray a little more than feathered ones.
A bowyer's drying rack. Lay green bow and longbow staves on its pegs to season them: 3 days for a bow stave, 5 for a longbow stave. Seasoned wood makes a stronger bow.

A grapple and a coil of rope. Shoot it through an open or broken upstairs window, or high on the wall right beside one, and it hangs a rope down to the ground that you can climb: no stairs needed. Heavy: it doesn't fly far.
Seasoned on a stave rack: a bow made from it hits harder, reaches farther and wears slower.

A Blasting Arrow with nails taped round the charge. It explodes where it strikes like a Blasting Arrow, and throws nails out to about 5 tiles, wounding or killing what stands further off. Very loud. The fuze arms after about 5 tiles. Used up when it goes off.

A smoke mix wrapped behind the point. Light it first, like a fire arrow: where it lands it pours out thick smoke about 3 tiles across for a while, and zombies caught in it lose track of what they were after. It never starts a fire. Unlit, it's a dud.

A Blasting Arrow on a crafted timer, with glue on its nose. It sticks in whatever it hits and goes off about 5 seconds later, wherever that zombie has walked to; it beeps while it counts down. A miss goes off where it lands. Used up when it goes off.

A flashlight taped to an arrow shaft. Attach it to any bow or crossbow: it sits on the bow like a stabilizer and lights where you aim. Turn it on and off with the light key or from the reload menu. Takes batteries; unstrap it to get the flashlight back.
Folded tape fletching: quick and needs no tools, but arrows fletched with it stray more and wear out fast. Not good enough for a matched set.
Load a game first, then equip a bow and press Check compatibility again.
Full report: %1 (in your Zomboid folder; also in console.txt, lines starting [Fletcher diag]). Share it in a comment on Fletcher's Workshop page.
Advanced lob shots (power by draw time)

Lob shots get their power from you: hold the Lob Shot key (controller: D-pad up) while aiming and the power builds (a meter shows it by the reticle). More power sends the arrow higher and steeper onto the same spot, longer in the air; too little falls short of the white mark. In first / third person (ViewPoint), tap the key (controller: D-pad down) on a spot to mark it, then look up: the meter's green band is the power that lands there. Your Archery level steadies the power, and a stronger lob hits harder. Off: Fletcher picks the arc for you.

Bow invisible, wrong animations, stuck after a shot? Equip a bow, then press this: Fletcher checks what it needs from the game and your other mods, shows what it found, and writes a report to Zomboid/Lua/Fletcher_diagnostics.txt to share with the mod author.
Lights the fire arrow on your bow (with a lighter or matches). Tapping the reload key again does the same.

Hold while you shoot a bow or crossbow: the arrow goes up and over what's in the way (a tall fence, a wall, a car) and comes down on the spot under your reticle. K is a free key (vanilla leaves it unbound). Controllers: hold the Controller Lob Button (D-pad up unless you change it below) while aiming.

While aiming, a dashed line shows where your arrow would go if you shot now (without the shot's spread): white for a normal shot, blue through an upstairs window, orange for a lob. A red mark where it would stop, green on a zombie. A practice and testing aid: off by default.
The streak and the thin line that follow a flying arrow. Turn off to see the arrow alone. Only changes what you see.

A note over your character each time you gain Archery XP (a hit, a kill, target practice, a tape), with the amount you really got. Skills without a boost from your profession or traits gain a quarter of the XP.

On a controller, hold this while you aim a bow or crossbow to lob the shot. It only takes the button while you aim a Fletcher launcher; the rest of the time it does what it always did. Pick another button if you use the D-pad while aiming for something else, or Off.

On a controller with advanced lob shots in ViewPoint's view: tap this while aiming to mark the spot under the crosshair (tap at the sky to clear it). Only taken while you aim a Fletcher launcher. If it's the same as the lob button, the lob button wins.
Grew up shooting a bow and making their own arrows. Draws, steadies and nocks faster from day one.
